questions.q: What does 'verification' mean in a resolution note?
options: Asking the user if they are happy with the response
The specific check performed that proves the fix actually worked, such as re-running a process
A guess about whether the fix probably worked
questions.explain: Verification is a concrete, repeatable check — like re-running Validate and confirming the invoice reaches Validated status — not an assumption.

questions.q: Put these ticket stages in the correct order: Resolve, Triage, Investigate, Intake.
questions.explain: The six stages run Intake, Triage, Reproduce and Scope, Investigate, Resolve, Document and Close.

questions.q: Where would you look first to find out why a specific invoice is blocked from payment?
options: The Holds or Review tab on the invoice
questions.explain: Holds and Review tabs in Payables show exactly which rule placed a hold on a specific transaction.

questions.q: Which hold would most likely be triggered if an invoice's tax amount does not match what Oracle calculates from the configured tax rate?
questions.explain: A Tax Variance hold is specifically for cases where the invoice's tax amount doesn't match the amount calculated from the configured tax rate.

questions.q: What are the four stages a Payment Process Request moves through?
questions.explain: A PPR moves through Select (gather eligible invoices), Build (construct payment documents), Format (produce the bank file), and Confirm (finalize the payment).

questions.q: Why does the resolution note explicitly state 'No setup change was required'?
options: Because Oracle requires that exact phrase on every ticket
Because setup changes are never allowed in production support
So a future reader doesn't assume a tolerance or validation rule was altered for all suppliers
questions.explain: Stating that no setup changed clarifies the fix was isolated to this one invoice's data, not a rule affecting other transactions.

questions.q: What parameters shape which transactions appear on a given customer statement run?
options: A statement cycle and date range (cutoff), which determine which customers and transactions are included
The GL chart of accounts structure
questions.explain: A statement run is shaped by cycle and date-range parameters that define exactly which transactions, as of a cutoff, are included.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of the $9,000 gap at Harbor & Vance Logistics?
options: A manual journal was posted directly to the AR control account in GL instead of being entered as a Receivables transaction
questions.explain: A $9,000 manual journal was posted straight to the AR control account in GL, bypassing Receivables entirely, so the subledger never reflected it.

questions.q: Why are the 3 outstanding check lines not actually a problem to fix?
options: Because outstanding checks should always be deleted
Because the bank already rejected those checks
Because they are a normal timing difference — checks issued and recorded, but not yet cleared by the bank
questions.explain: Outstanding checks remaining unreconciled until the bank clears them is expected and correct — 'not yet reconciled' is not the same thing as 'broken.'

questions.q: What is the Close Monitor / period close checklist used for?
options: Showing exactly which specific prerequisites are met or outstanding before a period can close
questions.explain: Rather than a single opaque 'can't close' message, the Close Monitor identifies precisely which prerequisites (like unposted journals or untransferred subledger batches) remain outstanding.

questions.q: What was the recommended process improvement in the resolution note?
options: Enable suspense posting for every ledger
Require all journals to be entered manually going forward
Have the chart-of-accounts cleanup project circulate disabled account values to GL accountants before disabling them
questions.explain: The note recommends proactively notifying GL accountants of accounts being disabled, to catch any transactions still coded to them before they cause a posting failure.

questions.q: What is the Accounting Event Diagnostic report used for?
options: Showing exactly what source data SLA referenced (and didn't find a rule for) while attempting to create a journal entry
questions.explain: This report is specifically useful for diagnosing cases where an SLA accounting rule or source data didn't match what the Create Accounting process expected.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of all six delivery truck lines being stuck On Hold?
options: The trucks were not yet delivered
The new asset category 'Vehicles - Delivery Trucks' had no depreciation expense account defined for the book, so no line using that category could derive one
questions.explain: A single category-level setup gap (missing expense account) affected every line using that category, which is why all six were held for the same reason.

questions.q: What determines whether a user can see a page or function at all, like Manage Invoices?
options: The job role and its bundled function privileges
questions.explain: Job roles and their function privileges control whether a page or function is visible/usable at all, separate from which data it can act on.

questions.q: What did the BPM Worklist routing history reveal about the stuck report?
options: It was rejected by the manager
It had already been approved but not updated
The approval process never successfully assigned a next approver, so nothing was pending with anyone
questions.explain: The routing history showed the approval process failed to build a complete approver chain, leaving the report with no pending task assigned to anyone.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of the $340,000 difference between the Balance Sheet report and Smart View?
options: The Balance Sheet report ran at 7:00 AM, before a Mass Additions batch posted at 7:45 AM; Smart View was refreshed after the batch posted
questions.explain: Both figures were accurate for the moment they were generated — the report simply ran before new equipment had posted into the active asset register, while Smart View reflected the later state.

questions.q: What type of error pointed toward a version mismatch rather than a data problem in this ticket?
questions.explain: An integrity check failure on the workbook/integration itself (rather than a specific data field) pointed toward a client/server version mismatch, not a data issue.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of the sudden 400 errors on the Invoices REST resource?
options: The integration team changed their authentication token
A quarterly Oracle Fusion update changed the resource so BusinessUnit became a required field on the request, where it had previously defaulted server-side
questions.explain: An Oracle-side update changed the resource's required-field behavior, which is why the integration team's own code appeared unchanged yet started failing.
